title: The proposed strict native fraction package is false on nonempty schemes
statement: Fix a finite field k0, a prime l, and a nonempty k0-scheme X. Let T be any additive bifunctor on native pro-etale Weil sheaves, with the additive partial functors and sum totals used in NativeTensorKFlat [def-sf-native-weil-tensor-presentation]. The conjunction of a strict right calculus of fractions for quasi-isomorphisms on native cochain complexes and K-flat replacement density is false. This refutes the current package without disputing actual K-flat replacement for the normalized tensor. The refutation is independent of the distinct-characteristic assumption in the original section.

source.place: Tag 014D, cone of an identity and its termwise split inclusion; Tag 04VC, RMS3 cancellation.

proof.text: Assume the proposed conjunction and retain its first conjunct. Apply the general cone obstruction to the single complex of the native constant coefficient sheaf in degree zero. It is acyclic.

The zeroth homology of a single complex is its sole term, so the native constant sheaf would be zero. Forget Frobenius and then adic module structure. These additive functors preserve zero objects. This makes the ordinary adic constant coefficient sheaf zero.

The geometric fiber of a nonempty scheme over k0 is nonempty (Scheme.Hom.nonempty_geometricFiber). The constant coefficient sheaf there has nonzero section 1, as proved by ProEtale.not_isZero_adicConstantSheaf. This contradiction refutes the package. On an empty scheme the nonzero-section argument is unavailable, exactly as the Nonempty hypothesis records.

lean.statement:
theorem native_weil_tensor_ringed_kflat_resolution_obstruction [Nonempty X] :
    ¬ (let W₀ := HomologicalComplex.quasiIso
        (ProEtaleWeilSheaf k₀ l X) (.up ℤ)
      W₀.HasRightCalculusOfFractions ∧
        let P : ObjectProperty (CochainComplex (ProEtaleWeilSheaf k₀ l X) ℤ) :=
          NativeTensorKFlat k₀ l X T
        ∀ L : CochainComplex (ProEtaleWeilSheaf k₀ l X) ℤ,
          ∃ (P' : P.FullSubcategory) (s : P.ι.obj P' ⟶ L), W₀ s)
